items.title: IRGC warns states hosting US forces of 'corresponding response'
items.summary: IRGC warns states hosting US forces of 'corresponding response' Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has warned countries hosting US military forces to prepare for a "corresponding response", Iranian media reported. In a statement carried by Tasnim News Agency, the IRGC urged those countries to "activate their civil defence units to protect their citizens and move them away from potential military targets". The Guard said the countries were being used as "launchpads for aggression against Iran". The IRGC also claimed it had used drones and missiles to target a US military logistics hub at Camp Arifjan in Kuwait and had disabled the radar system at the US' Ali Al Salem Air Base in the country. Iranian officials said at least eight civilians were killed in US strikes in the Hormuzgan province on Friday, and several others were injured.

items.title: India-linked ships among top Hormuz transit users, MarineTraffic says
items.summary: India-linked ships among top Hormuz transit users, MarineTraffic says Vessels travelling to and from India accounted for one of the largest shares of applications to use Iran-designated routes through the Strait of Hormuz, according to MarineTraffic. Citing the data released by Iran, MarineTraffic said that in the three weeks following the 17 June US-Iran peace memorandum, India-bound ships accounted for 20 percent of outbound transit requests, second only to China at 21 percent. For vessels entering the Gulf, India was the largest country of origin, representing 21 percent of requests. MarineTraffic said Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA) reported receiving more than 200 transit permits and insurance applications from non-Iranian vessels during the period. Tankers accounted for 41 percent of requests, followed by bulk carriers at 27 percent and container ships at 18 percent.

items.title: Iran suspends agreement with Washington after 'US violations'
items.summary: Iran suspends agreement with Washington after 'US violations' Iran's deputy foreign minister, Kazem Gharibabadi, said Tehran had suspended its commitments to the memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Washington as US attacks continue. “The US has violated and suspended all its commitments within the framework of the Islamabad MoU,” Gharibabadi said. The deputy foreign minister added that Tehran had suspended its commitments under the agreement as it is "busy defending the country".

items.title: US strikes on Iran’s Hormozgan province kill eight people: Report
items.summary: US strikes on Iran’s Hormozgan province kill eight people: Report Local Iranian media have reported that US attacks on Iran’s southern Hormozgan province over the past two nights killed “about seven to eight people”, all of them civilians, according to Ahmad Moradi, a representative for the province who spoke to Iran’s Tasnim news agency. Tasnim reported that one strike targeted a bridge in the province, hitting two family cars and killing six people. The agency also said the Tappeh Allah-o-Akbar neighbourhood in Bandar Abbas was struck, killing a woman and leaving a one-year-old child with an amputated limb. It added that a driver delivering fuel to petrol stations was killed in a fire.

items.title: Iranian official says US strikes disrupt water supply to 20 villages
items.summary: Iranian official says US strikes disrupt water supply to 20 villages Drinking water supply to 20 villages with a population of nearly 10,000 has been disrupted after US strikes damaged water desalination pumps in the coastal Bunji village, in Iran’s Jask county, according to Abdolhamid Hamzehpour, the CEO of the Hormozgan Water and Wastewater Company. Iran’s Tasnim agency quoted Hamzehpour as referring to the US strikes as “a series of crimes and terrorist attacks”. He said a pumping station for extracting water from the sea and a power transformer at the Bunji desalination plant were “completely destroyed”.

items.title: Kuwait Airways says most flights rescheduled as airspace closed
items.summary: Kuwait Airways says most flights rescheduled as airspace closed Kuwait Airways has rescheduled most of its flights due to the airspace closure on Saturday, the airline said in a post on X. "Kuwait Airways urges all passengers to stay updated on their flight status. Notifications and text messages will be sent to the phone numbers registered with their bookings to inform them of any updates," the post read. Earlier, the Kuwaiti army said it was responding to Iranian missile and drone attacks for the third time and urged the people to “adhere to the authorities’ safety and security instructions”. #kuwait_airways announces to its valued customers the rescheduling of most flights due to the airspace closure on Saturday, 18 July 2026. items.title: Iran strikes: Jordan intercepts 10 missiles, Bahrain sounds sirens
items.summary: Iran strikes: Jordan intercepts 10 missiles, Bahrain sounds sirens The Jordanian military has said its air defences downed 10 Iranian missiles that breached the country’s airspace early on Saturday morning. The military said the interceptions caused no casualties or material damage, and Royal Engineers have begun clearing and securing debris from the impact sites. Iran’s IRNA posted on X “footage demonstrating Iranian missiles breaching Jordan's air defence networks and rendering the US Patriot systems entirely ineffective”. CBS News, citing officials, said that several American service members were injured in Iranian attacks on Jordanian bases this week. Bahrain, meanwhile, sounded sirens for the third time in just a few hours, with officials urgently advising residents to take cover immediately.
